description: Three phrasal movements whose claims name the moving occurrence under an open field (mover), its lower occurrence as trace, and the head that attracts it as target: eppMovement {mover: e_she, trace: e_shetr, target: e_t} (sixth stage), operatorMovement {mover: e_obj, trace: e_objtr, target: e_than} (seventh stage) and eppMovement {mover: m_rosa, trace: m_rosatr, target: m_t} (fourteenth stage). Each mover keeps its ID at the landing and its new trace holds the exact preceding slot. Recognition took the target head as the landing, found no shared lineage with the trace (MOVEMENT_LINEAGE_UNPROVEN) and drew gap badges with no arrow. The kept-ID occurrence is now the landing and the attracting head stays context, as when a target field names the landing. Test input for tests/keptLandingAttractingHead.test.mjs; kept out of fixtures/ because its agree plaque at e_t sits beyond its nearby reach on main (1.29) and with this fix (1.38), the far-plaque family ROADMAP lists as not active.
source: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), high effort, Anthropic Messages API qualification run (npm run qualification:anthropic) under contract commit 35e88f0, 29 October 2026 (held-out batch heldout-20261029, run h1-023-en-pseudogapping, analysis 1 of 1). Tokens are the model’s own final words.
sentence: Rosa gave more money to the school than she did to the hospital.

derivationStages.statement: The compared nominal of the than-clause, a silent degree operator with 'much money', is assembled.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Comparative deletion here is treated as movement of the whole compared constituent. So the than-clause starts from a full nominal that parallels the matrix 'more money', but its degree slot is filled by a silent operator rather than by the comparative morpheme. The operator merges with the quantity head 'much', and the result merges with the noun 'money'. The degreeArgument relation records that the operator saturates the degree argument of 'much'. This is what later lets the clause denote a degree description, roughly 'the amount x such that she gave x-much money to the hospital'.

derivationStages.statement: The goal phrase 'to the hospital' of the than-clause is built as a separate object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The determiner 'the' merges with 'hospital', and the preposition 'to' merges with that phrase. The resulting goal phrase sits in the workspace beside the compared nominal. It will become the pseudogapping remnant that contrasts with 'to the school', so it is built before the verb that selects it. No non-structural relation is established yet.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded lexical verb 'give' forms a Larsonian VP with its goal and theme.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb 'give' first merges with the goal phrase 'to the hospital' and assigns it the goal role. The resulting verbal object then merges with the compared nominal, which takes the theme role in the higher position. This ditransitive shell mirrors the one the matrix clause will build. The first thetaAssignment relation links 'give' to the goal phrase, and the second links 'give' to the compared nominal as theme.

derivationStages.statement: Light v merges, 'give' raises to v, and the subject 'she' is merged as agent.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges with the VP. The verb 'give' then raises and adjoins to it, leaving a silent trace inside the VP. This is the same head movement that will give 'gave more money' its order in the matrix clause. After that, the pronoun 'she' is externally merged at the edge of the v projection. The headMovement relation connects the raised verb, its trace and the host light verb. The thetaAssignment relation then records that the light verb assigns the agent role to 'she'.

derivationStages.statement: A Focus head above vP attracts the remnant 'to the hospital' out of the future ellipsis site.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Pseudogapping leaves 'to the hospital' pronounced while the rest of the verb phrase goes unpronounced. So the remnant must escape the verb phrase before ellipsis. A silent Focus head merges with the v projection. It carries a contrastive-focus feature and also the ellipsis feature that will later license deletion of its complement. The goal phrase then moves from its VP-internal position to the specifier of Focus, leaving a silent trace. The focusMovement relation links the moved goal phrase, its trace and the attracting Focus head.

derivationStages.statement: Past T, spelled out as 'did', agrees with 'she', and 'she' raises to the T edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Past tense T merges above the Focus phrase. The verb complex is buried below Focus and inside the soon-to-be-elided verb phrase, so tense cannot be realized on the verb. T is therefore spelled out by do-support as 'did'. T first probes and agrees with the subject 'she' for phi-features and nominative case. 'She' then raises to the specifier of T, leaving a silent trace in the agent position. The doSupport relation records that past tense on T is realized as 'did'. The agree relation links T to 'she'. The epp movement relation links the raised 'she', its trace and T.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer 'than' merges and the operator-bearing nominal moves to its specifier, forming the than-clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The complementizer 'than' merges with the T phrase. Its operator feature attracts the compared nominal containing the degree operator. That nominal moves from the theme position to the specifier of 'than', leaving a silent trace in the VP. The clause is thereby turned into a degree abstraction. At this point the moved nominal still carries its own phonology. Its deletion depends on the matrix antecedent, which is not yet in the workspace. The operatorMovement relation links the moved nominal, its trace and the complementizer 'than'.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix object 'more money' is built with the comparative morpheme selecting the than-clause, and comparative deletion applies.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The comparative degree head '-er' merges with the than-clause as its complement. The resulting degree phrase merges with the quantity head 'much', and that phrase merges with 'money', giving the matrix theme. The comparativeSelection relation records that '-er' selects the than-clause as its standard of comparison. The degreeArgument relation records that the degree phrase saturates the degree argument of matrix 'much'. The comparativeDeletion relation then links the fronted compared nominal of the than-clause to its antecedents, matrix 'much' and 'money'. Because the two are identical, the fronted nominal becomes silent, which is why no 'much money' is heard after 'than'.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix goal phrase 'to the school' is built alongside the matrix object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The determiner 'the' merges with 'school', and 'to' merges with the result. This gives the matrix goal phrase, the correlate of the focused remnant 'to the hospital'. It remains a separate object next to the matrix theme. No non-structural relation is established here.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix 'gave' forms a Larsonian VP with goal 'to the school' and theme 'more money'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb 'gave' merges first with 'to the school' and assigns it the goal role. The verbal object then merges with 'more money', which receives the theme role. This builds the same shell as in the than-clause, which is what makes the later ellipsis parallel. The two thetaAssignment relations link 'gave' to the goal phrase and then to the theme.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix light v merges, 'gave' raises to it, and 'Rosa' is merged as agent.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges with the matrix VP. 'Gave' raises to it, leaving a silent trace, so the verb now precedes 'more money' as in the surface order. 'Rosa' is then externally merged at the v edge. The headMovement relation links the raised 'gave', its trace and the host light verb. The thetaAssignment relation records that the light verb assigns the agent role to 'Rosa'.

derivationStages.statement: The than-clause extraposes from the degree phrase and right-adjoins to the matrix vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The than-clause leaves its base position as complement of '-er' and right-adjoins to the matrix v projection, leaving a silent trace inside 'more money'. This movement does three things for this sentence. It places 'than she did to the hospital' after 'to the school'. It marks the matrix vP as the scope of the comparative. It also lifts the future ellipsis site out of the matrix vP that will serve as its antecedent, so no antecedent-containment problem arises. The extraposition relation links the moved than-clause, its trace and the matrix vP it adjoins to.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded vP is elided under identity with the matrix vP, and 'to the hospital' is set in contrast with 'to the school'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: With the matrix vP now available as an antecedent outside the than-clause, the ellipsis feature on the embedded Focus head deletes its complement. The deleted complement is the embedded v projection containing the traces of 'give', 'she', the compared nominal and the goal phrase. This yields the pseudogapping string 'she did to the hospital'. The vpEllipsis relation links the licensing Focus head, the elided embedded vP and its matrix vP antecedent. The contrastiveFocus relation then pairs the surviving remnant 'to the hospital' with its matrix correlate 'to the school'. This contrast is the parallelism that licenses the focus-driven escape of the remnant.

derivationStages.statement: Silent past T merges in the matrix, values past tense on 'gave', agrees with 'Rosa', and 'Rosa' raises.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent past-tense T merges with the matrix v projection, including the adjoined than-clause. No auxiliary intervenes, so tense is realized on the raised verb, as 'gave', rather than by do-support. The tenseValuation relation records that T values past tense on the verb complex. The agree relation links T to 'Rosa' for phi-features and nominative case. 'Rosa' then raises to the specifier of T, leaving a silent trace. The eppMovement relation links the raised 'Rosa', its trace and T.

derivationStages.statement: A silent declarative C completes the sentence, and '-er' with 'much' is spelled out as 'more'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative complementizer merges with the matrix T phrase, completing the clause. At spell-out, the comparative degree head and the quantity head 'much' are realized together by the suppletive form 'more'. They stay separate in the syntax because '-er' alone selects the than-clause and 'much' alone parallels the deleted 'much' of the compared nominal. The morphologicalRealization relation establishes this joint spell-out of '-er' and 'much' as 'more'.
